plan.topic: Having surgery, an endoscopy or a procedure while on semaglutide or tirzepatide: a checklist of what to tell your care team (hook: Oct 12 systematic review on blood-sugar control around cardiac surgery in adults with T2D)
plan.angle:
Hook on GLIMPSE, not the unverified cardiac-surgery review. Title: 'Surgery or Endoscopy on Semaglutide or Tirzepatide? 4 Things to Tell Your Care Team'.
Slide 1: the question.
Slide 2: 'These medicines can slow stomach emptying (label wording). In a 2025 UK study of 47,000+ adults having anaesthesia, regurgitation or aspiration was recorded in 1.41% of people who'd used a GLP-1-based medicine in the past 3 months vs 0.12% of non-users (19 of 1,348 vs 57 of 45,691). Most events were regurgitation. The study shows a link, not proof of cause.' Source tag: GLIMPSE.
Slide 3: tell your anesthesia team and prescriber which medicine you take and when you last took it.
Slide 4: mention any nausea, vomiting or fullness in the days before.
Slide 5: 'If you have diabetes, ask how your blood sugar will be managed around the procedure.' Use no source tag unless it cites a confirmed guideline.
Slide 6: 'Guidance differs between professional groups. Follow your team's plan, and don't stop or change your medicine on your own.'
Slide 7: 'talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you'.
A source tag on every claim slide, using direct canonical URLs.
plan.working_title: Surgery on Semaglutide or Tirzepatide? 5 Things to Tell Your Care Team
plan.why:
It turns our #3 GLP-1 post (anesthesia, 82 views) into a checklist format people save. The hook is the systematic review published Oct 12. | fact-check: GLIMPSE is verified (UK, 119 hospitals, Sept–Dec 2025, led by Kariem El-Boghdadly). Regurgitation or aspiration occurred in 19 of 1,348 people who had used a GLP-1-based medicine in the previous 3 months (1.41%) vs 57 of 45,691 non-users (0.12%). Of the 19 events, 17 were regurgitation and 2 were pulmonary aspiration. It is an observational association.
I could NOT verify the 'Oct 12 systematic review on blood-sugar control around cardiac surgery in adults with T2D'. What I found on GLP-1s in cardiac surgery concerns giving liraglutide around surgery as a glucose-control tool, which is a different question from patients already on semaglutide or tirzepatide. Drop it as the hook unless the exact paper is confirmed, and don't let slide 5 imply that GLP-1s should be used or continued around surgery.
The title says '5 Things', but the checklist has 4 action slides (3–6). Make the count match.
No stopping, pausing or timing advice is correct. 'Say when you last took it' is fine because it's information-giving.
Note: the playbook says carousels are dead (Instagram reach 0–3, n=15) and recommends rebuilding this exact topic as a Short. That's the owner's call, but the content is approvable either way.

package.title: Surgery or Endoscopy on Semaglutide or Tirzepatide? 4 Things to Tell Your Care Team

social.instagram_caption:
Having surgery or an endoscopy while on semaglutide or tirzepatide? Your care team needs to know.

Here's why:
• Both US drug labels say to tell your providers before any planned surgery or procedure
• These medicines delay stomach emptying — rare after-approval reports describe food left in the stomach under general anesthesia or deep sedation despite reported fasting
• A UK study (GLIMPSE, 47,039 adults under anaesthetic care) found regurgitation or aspiration in 1.41% of people who used a GLP-1-based medicine in the past 3 months (19 of 1,348) vs 0.12% of non-users (57 of 45,691). That's a link, not proof of cause: obesity and diabetes, also risk factors, were more common in GLP-1 users
• Guidance differs between professional groups, so ask your own team what their plan is

Swipe for the 4 things to tell them: your medicine + last dose, any nausea/vomiting/fullness, whether you have diabetes, and ask for their plan. Follow it, and don't stop or change your medicine on your own.

Send this to someone with a procedure coming up.

factcheck.summary: The carousel is accurate and safe. I checked the GLIMPSE figures against the EurekAlert release dated Sept 16, 2026: 47,039 adults at 119 UK sites; GLP-1 use in the 3 months before the procedure; 19 of 1,348 (1.41%, 1 in 71) vs 57 of 45,691 (0.12%, 1 in 802); 17 regurgitation and 2 aspiration. The release also says obesity and diabetes are over-represented in GLP-1 users. All of this matches the carousel, and slide 3 correctly frames it as a link, not proof of cause. The Mounjaro label (revised 8/2026) says it 'delays gastric emptying', describes 'rare postmarketing reports of pulmonary aspiration… despite reported adherence to preoperative fasting recommendations', and tells clinicians to 'instruct patients to inform healthcare providers prior to any planned surgeries or procedures'. The FDA copy of the Ozempic label says the same things. The 2024 multisociety guidance (ASA, AGA, ASMBS, ISPCOP, SAGES) exists, says most patients may continue their GLP-1, and calls for individual risk assessment that includes GI symptoms. That supports both the 'no one-size-fits-all rule' and the 'don't stop or change on your own' messages. The prescriber line is present, and there is no dosing, hold-time or stopping advice. I found only minor wording and source-list fixes.

issues.claim: After-approval reports, under anesthesia or deep sedation, despite fasting
issues.problem: The label's wording is 'who had residual gastric contents despite reported adherence to preoperative fasting recommendations'. 'Despite fasting' drops the word 'reported' and the residual stomach contents, so it says slightly more than the label does.
issues.fix: Change detail to: "After-approval reports under general anesthesia or deep sedation: food left in the stomach despite reported fasting"

issues.problem: Tirzepatide comes only as an injection. Only semaglutide has tablet forms (Rybelsus, Wegovy pill), and neither tablet label is in the source list. As written, it suggests both medicines come as tablets.
issues.fix: Change detail to: "Weekly injection, or a semaglutide tablet"

issues.claim: In the days before your procedure. 2024 multisociety guidance ... lists stomach symptoms among the factors teams weigh before anesthesia.
issues.problem: The guidance asks teams to assess GI symptoms before the procedure, including on the day. 'In the days before' adds a timeframe the guidance doesn't state.
issues.fix: Change body to: "Before your procedure, including on the day. 2024 multisociety guidance (ASA, AGA, ASMBS, ISPCOP, SAGES) lists stomach symptoms among the factors teams weigh before anesthesia."

issues.problem: The body says 'under anaesthetic care', but the headline drops the UK population. Most events happened while patients were waking up from anesthesia.
issues.fix: Change headline to: "Regurgitation or aspiration around anesthesia (UK study)"

issues.claim: OZEMPIC Full Prescribing Information, Novo Nordisk, 2025, novo-pi.com/ozempic.pdf
issues.problem: This is a living label, and a 2026 FDA revision exists, so the 2025 year is out of date. The novo-pi PDF also didn't return readable text when fetched. The FDA copy confirms the cited wording.
issues.fix: Replace with: {"id":"S2","title":"OZEMPIC (semaglutide) injection — Prescribing Information","publisher":"Novo Nordisk / US FDA","year":"2026","url":"https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/209637s038lbl.pdf"}

issues.problem: The source is a press release, not the paper itself, and the slide cites 'Anaesthesia, 2026'. That's acceptable, but the release date should be in the title.
issues.fix: Change S1 title to: "Peri-operative glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use and outcomes: a national prospective multicentre cohort study (GLIMPSE) — news release, 16 Sep 2026"
